name: Gabapentin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 300 mg day 1, 600 mg/day day 2, 900 mg/day day 3; titrate up to 1800 mg/day in 3 doses
300 mg 3 times daily; may titrate to 600 mg 3 times daily

key_interactions.effect: Respiratory depression and sedation, sometimes fatal; morphine raises gabapentin levels.
key_interactions.action: Watch for somnolence, sedation and respiratory depression; gabapentin dose may need adjustment.
Take gabapentin at least 2 hours after the antacid.

key_interactions.effect: False positives with Ames N-Multistix SG.

common: Postherpetic neuralgia: dizziness, somnolence, peripheral edema (≥8% and at least twice placebo)
Epilepsy, over 12 years: somnolence, dizziness, ataxia, fatigue, nystagmus
serious: Seizures or status epilepticus after abrupt withdrawal
Neuropsychiatric reactions in children 3 to 12 years

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to gabapentin or its ingredients
monitoring: Sedation, dizziness and respiratory status, especially with opioids or kidney impairment

pk.bioavailability: About 60% at 900 mg/day, falling to 27% at 4800 mg/day (not dose proportional)
pk.half_life_eskd: About 52 hours at CrCl <30 mL/min; about 132 hours in anuric adults on non-dialysis days (label)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: Renal excretion as unchanged drug (primary route)
pk.dialyzability: Yes: half-life falls to about 3.8 hours during hemodialysis (label).
